title: Keep the runtime base64 regexes linear so composed parse paths cannot overflow
body:
Fixes the finding from the #6528 review: `z.templateLiteral(["id-", z.base64url()]).safeParse` threw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on multi-megabyte input. The quantified block forms (`(?:[...]{4})*`) recurse per block in V8's regex engine, so ~8M chars overflows the stack. `z.base64()` and `z.base64url()` were already mitigated internally, but template literals compose member `def.pattern`s and test them on every parse.

The split, reworked per review: the public `z.regexes.base64` and `z.regexes.base64url` keep their strict shipped semantics and are untouched. The lax linear forms (`/^[0-9a-zA-Z+/]*={0,2}$/`, `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/`) live module-local in `schemas.ts` and become `def.pattern` for the two formats — parse validation is unchanged because `isValidBase64`/`isValidBase64URL` enforce the length rules. The JSON Schema emitter swaps the lax patterns back to the strict exports by reference, at both consumer sites: `stringProcessor`'s `pattern`/`allOf` and `recordProcessor`'s `patternProperties` (the review caught that `z.looseRecord(z.base64url(), …)` would otherwise emit the lax key — now pinned by a test). `toJSONSchema(z.base64url())` still emits the length-aware pattern from #6527; its snapshot and agreement tests pass unchanged, and `base64` gains the symmetric agreement test. `templateLiteralProcessor` is deliberately left lax: its emitted pattern then agrees with the (length-lax) composed parse.

This also fixes a second bug the overflow investigation surfaced: `regexes.base64`'s leading `^$|` alternation leaked through template-literal composition, so on `main` `z.templateLiteral(["id-", z.base64()])` accepts `"AAAA"` with the prefix dropped and rejects the valid `"id-AAAA"`. Both directions are now pinned by a test. Composed base64url segments are length-lax again (`"id-A"` passes), as before #6527 — block length can't be meaningfully enforced mid-composition.

Verified with a controlled repro: on `main` the template-literal paths throw on 10MB input; on this branch they parse cleanly, and the big-input test now exercises them. Direct use of the strict `z.regexes.*` exports on multi-MB strings can still overflow — that's inherent to their quantified shape and out of scope here.

Axes: parse-path validator code is unchanged; template-literal parses get a simpler regex. Memory unchanged. Bundle, measured against `origin/main` with esbuild + gzip -9 on the treeshake fixtures: classic +47 B (classic retains the JSON Schema processors unconditionally via `processJSONSchema`), mini −2 B (mini shakes them until `toJSONSchema` is used).

reviews.body: Copilot was unable to review this pull request because the user who requested the review has reached their quota limit.

> [!IMPORTANT] > The identity-keyed pattern swap is applied in `stringProcessor` but not in `recordProcessor`, so `z.looseRecord(z.base64(), …)` now emits a `patternProperties` key that disagrees with parse — the same class of bug #6527 fixed. Details inline. **Reviewed changes** — full diff at `c199d32c`, plus the surrounding `regexes.*` / `bag.patterns` consumers, the JSON Schema processors, and a measured before/after of parse behavior, emitted patterns and bundle size. - **Runtime regexes go linear** — `regexes.base64` becomes `/^[0-9a-zA-Z+/]*={0,2}$/` and `regexes.base64url` becomes `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/`, removing the quantified block forms that overflow V8's regex stack at ~8M chars. - **Exact patterns move to the JSON Schema emitter** — a module-level `Map` keyed by object identity, swapped in at `stringProcessor`'s `patternList`. - **`isValidBase64URL` de-duplicates** — the private `base64urlCharset` added by #6527 is deleted in favor of `regexes.base64url`, whose source is now byte-identical. No behavior change. - **Big-input test extended** — the exported regexes and template-literal composition are now exercised on 10MB input; those four lines throw `RangeError` on `main`, so the test genuinely fails without the fix. Confirmed the core claim: `z.base64()` / `z.base64url()` parse is untouched (`def.pattern` is never tested for these formats, and `PATTERN_IS_COMPLETE` excludes them so AOT hoists the validator too), `z.hash(alg, { enc: "base64" })` resolves its own `md5_base64`-style regexes and is unaffected, and the four relevant test files pass. Worth noting the change also fixes a pre-existing bug it doesn't mention: on `main` the composed template-literal source for `["id-", z.base64()]` was `^id-$|^(?:[0-9a-zA-Z+/]{4})*…$`, whose top-level alternation leaked past its own segment, so `.parse("AAAA")` matched with the `id-` prefix dropped entirely. ### ⚠️ `z.regexes.base64` silently stops validating base64 structure for external consumers `z.regexes` is documented public API (`api.mdx` shows `z.string().regex(z.regexes.X)`), and `regexes.base64` has been strict in every released version. After this change `z.regexes.base64.test` flips `false` → `true` for `"A"`, `"AA"`, `"AAA"`, `"AAAAA"`, `"="`, `"=="`, `"A="` and `"AAAA=="` — anyone using it directly loses length and padding validation entirely, with no deprecation or release note. (`regexes.base64url` is not affected by this: it was already `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$/` before the unreleased #6527, so that half is a revert, not a regression.) The bundle argument doesn't force the choice, either — see the section below.
Technical details ````markdown # `z.regexes.base64` loses its structural guarantees ## Affected sites - `packages/zod/src/v4/core/regexes.ts:83` — public export weakened from the block-structured form to a charset-only form. ## Required outcome - Either `z.regexes.base64` keeps the semantics it has shipped with, or the weakening is stated explicitly in the PR body and release notes as a breaking change to a public export. ## Suggested approach (optional) - Invert the indirection instead of weakening the export: keep `regexes.base64` strict and public, add a module-local lax pattern used only for `def.pattern`, and key `exactPatterns` the other way (lax → `regexes.base64`). - This should shake identically on `zod/mini`, since the strict export would then be referenced only from `json-schema-processors.ts`, which mini drops unless `toJSONSchema` is called. Worth measuring before committing to it — I did not measure this variant. ## Open questions for the human - Is `z.regexes.base64` considered stable enough that a silent widening needs a release note, or is `z.base64()` the only contract that matters here? ````
### ℹ️ The pattern map is not actually behind `toJSONSchema` in classic The PR body says "the pattern map lives behind `toJSONSchema`, so shaking bundlers drop it for users who never call it". That holds for `zod/mini`, but not for classic: `classic/schemas.ts` imports `* as processors` at the top and all 42 constructors unconditionally assign `inst._zod.processJSONSchema = (…) => processors.XProcessor(…)`, so `json-schema-processors.ts` is reachable from every classic bundle whether or not `toJSONSchema` is used. Measured with esbuild (`bundle`, `minify`, `--conditions=@zod/source`) + gzip -9: classic pays **+67 raw / +42–46 gz unconditionally**, and a classic fixture that only uses `z.base64()` now also carries the base64url exact pattern it never references. Mini is genuinely unaffected (0, or −53 raw on a `z.base64()` fixture) unless `toJSONSchema` is called, in which case it is +140 raw / +75 gz rather than +2. The quoted numbers are roughly reproducible; it's the "opt-in" framing that isn't.
Technical details ````markdown # Bundle cost of `exactPatterns` is unconditional on classic ## Affected sites - `packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts:32-36` — new module-level `Map`. - `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/schemas.ts:4` and the 42 `processors.*Processor` closures — the reason the module is never shaken from classic. ## Required outcome - The PR body's bundle rationale should match what classic actually pays, so the tradeoff against the public-export weakening above is judged on real numbers. ## Suggested approach (optional) - No code change strictly required — ~45 B gz on classic is a defensible price. But since classic pays for both regex forms regardless, the bundle axis is not a reason to prefer weakening `z.regexes.base64` over keeping it strict. ````
### ℹ️ Nitpicks - `packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts:32` and `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/string.test.ts:296` are long capitalized multi-clause sentences. `CLAUDE.md` asks for "one lowercase sentence fragment, one clause, no trailing period" — the deleted `// charset only — the quantified regexes.base64url overflows…` was closer to the house register. - There's a `"base64url pattern agrees with parse"` test but no symmetric one for `base64`. Now that the emitted pattern for both formats reaches `toJSONSchema` through an indirection, the `base64` half is pinned only by an inline snapshot of the string, not by agreement with `safeParse`.   ｜ [Fix all ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6534?action=fix&review_id=5070267311) ｜ [Fix 👍s ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6534?action=fix-approved&review_id=5070267311) ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/actions/runs/33428772876/job/99608730327) ｜ Using `Claude Opus` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)

inline.body:
`stringProcessor` isn't the only consumer of `bag.patterns` — `recordProcessor`'s loose branch writes `pattern.source` straight into `patternProperties` with no `exactPatterns` lookup, so the swap misses it.

Measured on this branch: `z.looseRecord(z.base64(), z.number())` emits `patternProperties` keyed on `^[0-9a-zA-Z+/]*={0,2}$`, which matches `"A"`. Zod's loose record accepts `{ A: "not-a-number" }` (key isn't valid base64, so it's skipped), while the emitted schema requires that value to be a number — an external validator rejects input zod accepts. On `main` the emitted key was the exact pattern and didn't match `"A"`, so this is the `pattern`/parse disagreement #6527 removed, reintroduced through a different processor.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# `exactPatterns` swap misses `recordProcessor`

## Affected sites
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts:583` — `assignProp(json.patternProperties, pattern.source, valueSchema)` uses the raw (now lax) runtime regex.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/core/json-schema-processors.ts:57` — the only site currently applying the swap.

## Required outcome
- Every emitted JSON Schema construct derived from `bag.patterns` uses the exact block-structured form, not just `stringProcessor`'s `pattern` / `allOf`.
- A test pins it, so a future consumer of `bag.patterns` doesn't silently regress. `z.looseRecord(z.base64(), z.number())` currently has no coverage — `to-json-schema.test.ts`'s `patternProperties` tests all use `.regex(...)` keys.

## Suggested approach (optional)
- Hoist a one-liner next to the map and use it at both sites:

```ts
const exactPattern = (p: RegExp): RegExp => exactPatterns.get(p) ?? p;
```

- `stringProcessor`: `[...patterns].map(exactPattern)`; `recordProcessor`: `assignProp(json.patternProperties, exactPattern(pattern).source, valueSchema)`.

## Open questions for the human
- `templateLiteralProcessor` also reads a composed `_zod.pattern` and is deliberately left lax, which is correct — its emitted pattern then agrees with the (now length-lax) template-literal parse. Worth a line in the PR body so the asymmetry with `recordProcessor` is intentional on the record and not just on the template literal.
````

</details>

Nit, house style: this is three capitalized sentences on one line. Trimming to the constraint that actually explains the code keeps it in register — the JSON Schema half is already documented next to `exactPatterns`, and the `isValidBase64` half is documented at the validator.

```suggestion
// linear on purpose: the quantified block forms overflow the regex stack on multi-MB input, and these run on parse paths
```
